title: FD2: bounded flat-difference sieving with full-secret recovery

claims.statement: The single FD2 algorithm in proof.md Sections 1-10 has the following fixed configuration. For every integer N>=2 let n=ceil(log2 N), m=floor(log2 N), b=ceil(sqrt(n)), ell=ceil((m-1)/(b+1)) (ell=0 when m=1), J=m-1-ell, and clog(q)=ceil(log2 q), computed by the bit length of q-1. Set M=8192 clog(128(n+1)), F=2^(b+8)(n+1)^2+16M, L_i=32^(ell-i)F for 0<=i<=ell, R=8(n+1)L_0, A_coin=clog(256R), M_src=8192 clog(1024R(n+3)), and k_verify=n+8. All logarithms are base two. For every fixed s in Z/NZ, using only fresh independent challenge source states, FD2 returns the entire s with unconditional probability at least 251/256>2/3. Its total sequential work, including classical computation, addressing, circuit generation, all source copies, gates, measurement, resets and all attempts, is T(N,s)=O(R(n+1)^5+L_0(n+1)^4+(2^ell+2)(n+1)^4+1). Consequently T(N,s)=O(B_T(n)) uniformly over instances of bit length n, where B_T(n)=(n+1)^8 * 2^(6 ceil(sqrt(n))). The exact growth index g(B_T) is 1/2. All constants are absolute, independent of N, s and outcomes. This is the same program and parameter choice for all three resource claims; the total work and both allocated-space bounds hold jointly on every execution branch, including failures and aborts, under the fully charged classical bit-operation/Clifford+T model in rules.md.
